postmortem.what_happened: USD/MXN (Banxico FIX) rose from 19.3668 on 24 Nov to 19.704 on 25 Nov, extending a slide of about 5.5% in a week as a LatAm carry unwind, Fed hike pricing and US tariff reports hit high-yielders. The short peso position was closed after one day when the 24 Nov review flipped to a firmer peso after hot Mexican CPI, for a net gain of about 0.037%.
postmortem.assessment: The thesis that Banxico's cut had eroded carry against a hiking Fed was right in direction and in mechanism: the carry unwind was the driver. But the forecast was flipped the next day on a hot CPI print that the market ignored, so the decision to exit was the weaker one; the gain was a small, one-day result and partly luck in timing.
postmortem.do_differently: Give more weight to the global carry and positioning backdrop than to a single domestic data print when the two conflict; do not flip a one-point forecast on one release; track the LatAm FX cluster together as one call.
